# NVIDIA GPU profile catalog / GPU 配置目录

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_gpu_catalog.py; edit YAML profiles, then regenerate. -->

307 selectable configurations across 8 architectures and 16 CUDA compute capabilities. Counts include distinct memory/form-factor variants and synthetic profiles; they are not counts of unique GPU chips.

覆盖 Maxwell（GTX 900 时代）至 Blackwell（RTX 50 时代）。按游戏卡、数据中心、专业绘图顺序排列，桌面与笔记本、不同显存容量、PCIe/SXM 等使用独立 ID。涵盖已核实的公开配置，不把所有厂商超频版、OEM 定制版或未公开参数的 SKU 宣称为已穷尽。

## Reading specifications / 参数口径

- Each linked YAML is used by both Python and the native runtime. It contains memory capacity, SM count, bus width, clocks, L2 cache, CUDA shared-memory/register/thread limits, power fields, data types, sources, and notes.
- `reference` means public specification or an explicitly documented derivation; it does not mean physical calibration. `measured` and `synthetic` retain their existing meanings. Catalog support does not imply a matching CUDA toolkit or framework still supports an old GPU.
- `—` and a numeric zero in a reference specification mean unknown/unverified, not a hardware capacity of zero. `doctor --json` exposes `unavailable_fields`. Timing estimates reject profiles missing SM count, core clock, bus width, or memory clock.
- Memory capacity is expressed in GiB (nominal vendor GB is represented as binary capacity unless notes specify otherwise). Multi-GPU boards and superchips are represented per CUDA GPU, not by adding memory across devices.
- Memory MHz follows the existing analytical convention: half the effective per-pin data rate, so bandwidth in bytes/s = bus bits / 8 × memory MHz × 2,000,000. This may be derived from published bandwidth and is not necessarily the physical DRAM oscillator reported by a monitoring tool. Rounding can slightly change derived bandwidth.
- Core clocks are reference boost/operating clocks where documented. Mobile power and clocks depend on OEM configuration; the YAML notes identify reference envelopes. Power limit is a public reference ceiling when known, not measured typical consumption. CUDA shared-memory limits refer to usable shared memory, not the larger combined L1/shared cache.

## Coverage / 覆盖范围

| Architecture | Consumer | Data center | Workstation | Other |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Maxwell | 15 | 6 | 19 | 0 |
| Pascal | 23 | 6 | 22 | 0 |
| Volta | 1 | 8 | 1 | 0 |
| Turing | 24 | 1 | 21 | 0 |
| Ampere | 24 | 19 | 21 | 2 |
| Ada | 19 | 6 | 13 | 0 |
| Hopper | 0 | 14 | 0 | 0 |
| Blackwell | 17 | 7 | 17 | 1 |

Compute capability sources: [current NVIDIA table](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda/gpus), [legacy NVIDIA table](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda/gpus/legacy). These tables omit some mobile, regional, and memory variants; per-profile notes and source links supply additional evidence. The checked-in table snapshot is kept separate from researched profile specifications.

Research notes: [consumer](../docs/catalog-consumer-research.md), [data center](../docs/catalog-datacenter-research.md), [workstation](../docs/catalog-workstation-research.md). They describe source conflicts, derived parameters, and coverage boundaries.

```bash
python3 -m fakegpu doctor --list-profiles
python3 -m fakegpu doctor --profile gtx1660-super --json
FAKEGPU_PROFILE=rtx5090 python3 your_script.py
python3 scripts/render_gpu_catalog.py --check
```
